# Thermo property validation report (spec P1-05)

Generated 2026-11-10T03:28:10+00:00 from `data/validation/results.json` (git 1c4e31a1, CoolProp 8.0.0).
Regenerate with `uv run python scripts/validate_properties.py` and `--write-doc`.

## Tolerance policy (fixed before any result was seen)

| property | tolerance | basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| density (vapour) | 3 % relative | spec P1-05 |
| density (liquid) | 8 % relative | spec P1-05 — known cubic weakness |
| Cp | 5 % relative | spec P1-05 |
| bubble / dew pressure | 3 % relative | spec P1-05 |
| K-values | 5 % relative | spec P1-05 |
| NRTL MeOH/H2O bubble | 2 % relative | spec P1-05 (written for ethanol/water) |
| NRTL y | 0.02 absolute | spec P1-05 (written for ethanol/water) |
| bubble T (isobaric data) | 0.5 % relative | harness analogue of the 3 % bubble-P tolerance |
| phase compositions (liquid_comp) | 0.02 absolute | spec's composition tolerance |

- `kabadi-danner-free-water`: ok — n/a — l4_excluded: The L4 slice feed carries 0.3 % water, so its dew point at 293.15 K is the water dew point, which is what the free-water method moves: with the steam-table water fugacity the row's water dew lands at 933084 Pa against 615000-724000 Pa for the rows on EOS water, outside the 20 % band by construction. - `aq-c1h2o-310.9K-13.10MPa (kabadi-danner-free-water)` — liquid_comp -53.0% (0.00088856 vs 0.00189) - Kabadi-Danner SRK (documented rule, k_wj 0.5 + a'' term) under-predicts methane solubility at 310.9 K (-53 %), is close at 344.3 K (-9..-15 %) and over-predicts at 410.9 K (+44..+51 %): systematic temperature trend, also on n-hexane (Marche 2003). Note: Culberson & McKetta 1951 may be among the data Kabadi & Danner fitted (paper not retrievable), so these points are not counted as independent evidence. Model miss (measured 2026-11-09, aqueous).

- `aq-c1h2o-310.9K-13.10MPa (pr-free-water)` — liquid_comp -93.5% (0.00012295 vs 0.00189) - the free-water rule replaces only the water fugacity; methane keeps its EOS (k_ij = 0) fugacity in the water-rich liquid, so the solubility error is the host's (-93 % at 310.9 K, -78 % at 344.3 K, -9..-15 % at 410.9 K for PR) (measured 2026-11-09, aqueous).
- `aq-c1h2o-310.9K-13.10MPa (sour-pr)` — liquid_comp -93.5% (0.00012297 vs 0.00189) - host-EOS limit shared with the plain row (identical numbers to 4 digits: the ionisation correction acts only on H2S/CO2/NH3): one symmetric k_ij (0 for C1/H2O in the ChemSep table) cannot represent methane in the water-rich liquid; -93 % at 310.9 K, -78 % at 344.3 K, -9..-15 % at 410.9 K (measured 2026-11-09, aqueous).

- `chao-seader-c1c3-277.59K-4.826MPa` — K_C1 +6.7 % (3.063 vs 2.870); K_C3 passes (0.2490 vs 0.2602). The state lies outside the Chao-Seader recommended range (molal-average Tr 0.95 > 0.93 with methane present; Henley & Seader 1981 p. 189, restriction (d)). This K_C1 passed (2.889) only while methane carried omega_cs 0.011. Investigated 2026-11-04 (csgs): methane omega_cs corrected 0.011 -> 0 (Henley & Seader 1981 App. I p. 715); the implementation then reproduces an independent 1966 Chao-Seader implementation (Saxena thesis Table 5 p. 126, C1/nC5 at 310.93 K: K_C1 5.47 vs 5.49 at 3.447 MPa, 3.03 vs 3.04 at 6.895 MPa), so the deviation is the published correlation's. Model limitation, not a bug..
- `chao-seader-c1c3-294.26K-4.137MPa` — K_C1 +7.4 % (3.805 vs 3.542); K_C3 passes (0.3564 vs 0.3696). Molal-average Tr 0.945 > 0.93, outside the recommended range (Henley & Seader 1981 p. 189 (d)). This K_C1 passed (3.484) only while methane carried omega_cs 0.011. Investigated 2026-11-04 (csgs): methane omega_cs corrected 0.011 -> 0 (Henley & Seader 1981 App. I p. 715); the implementation then reproduces an independent 1966 Chao-Seader implementation (Saxena thesis Table 5 p. 126, C1/nC5 at 310.93 K: K_C1 5.47 vs 5.49 at 3.447 MPa, 3.03 vs 3.04 at 6.895 MPa), so the deviation is the published correlation's. Model limitation, not a bug..
- `cosmo-sac-ig-pure-H2O-370K` — Psat, rho_V and rho_L pass; Cp -12.2% (66.6483 vs 75.8833), the same value as the NRTL row's pure-H2O-370K-nrtl: the vapour-route liquid-Cp limitation, not COSMO-SAC (measured 2026-11-04).
- `cosmo-sac-ig-pure-MeOH-330K` — Psat and rho_L pass (74453.2 vs 74453.4 Pa, 755.904 vs 755.882 kg/m3); Cp -17.3% (73.1651 vs 88.5047) and rho_V -4.6% (0.869469 vs 0.911218) miss. Neither involves COSMO-SAC (gE = 0 for a pure liquid): the ideal-gas vapour ignores methanol's vapour non-ideality, and the vapour-route liquid enthalpy carries no residual liquid Cp - the gamma-phi limitation already assessed on the NRTL rows (measured 2026-11-04).

- `cpv-C1-155.0K` — bubble_P/dew_P +7.0 % (1295003 vs 1385690); rho_V -3.7 % (20.419 vs 19.657) — same PV-set Psat bias plus classical-EOS vapour density on the critical approach (measured 2026-11-04).
- `cpv-CO2-240.0K` — rho_V -3.3 % (33.295 vs 32.212) — classical (non-crossover) vapour density; Psat, rho_L, Cp pass (measured 2026-11-04).

- `gs-c1nc5-310.93K-1.379MPa (chao-seader)` — bubble_P -10.9 % (1.229 vs 1.379 MPa); y_C1 passes (0.8967 vs 0.8940). Investigated 2026-11-04 (csgs): methane omega_cs corrected 0.011 -> 0 (Henley & Seader 1981 App. I p. 715); the implementation then reproduces an independent 1966 Chao-Seader implementation (Saxena thesis Table 5 p. 126, C1/nC5 at 310.93 K: K_C1 5.47 vs 5.49 at 3.447 MPa, 3.03 vs 3.04 at 6.895 MPa), so the deviation is the published correlation's. Saxena's own comparison shows the same published CS prediction 7 % below the measured K_C1 at 3.447 MPa (5.49 vs 5.88). At 4.137 MPa K_C1 4.66 vs 4.93 (-5.6 %), K_nC5 0.0626 vs 0.0705 (-11 %, the Redlich-Kwong vapour fugacity of nC5, phi_V 0.526 vs PR 0.476). Model limitation, not a bug..
- `gs-c1nc5-310.93K-1.379MPa (grayson-streed)` — bubble_P -20.1 % (1.103 vs 1.379 MPa); y_C1 passes (0.8909 vs 0.8940) - Investigated 2026-11-04 (csgs): two data bugs fixed - methane omega_cs 0.011 -> 0 (Henley & Seader 1981 App. I p. 715; it had cut K_C1 by 11 %) and the GS simple-fluid A1 -2.10889 -> -2.10899 (H&S p. 188) - after which the implementation reproduces an independent 1966 Grayson-Streed implementation to its printed digits (Saxena thesis Table 5 p. 129, C1/nC4 at 310.93 K / 2.758 MPa: K_C1 5.73 vs 5.74, K_nC4 0.193 vs 0.193), and that published GS prediction is itself 15 % below the measured K_C1 6.75. At 310.93 K / 4.137 MPa both K stay low: K_C1 4.29 vs 4.93 (-13 %), K_nC5 0.0572 vs 0.0705 (-19 %); the GS pure-liquid nu0 of nC5 (0.0300) equals the PR pure-liquid f/P (0.0297), so the nC5 deficit is the correlation's Redlich-Kwong vapour fugacity of the heavy component (phi_V 0.526 vs PR 0.476). Model limitation of a correlation fitted for hydrogen-rich hydrotreater service, not a bug; lee-kesler-ploecker reproduces the 4.137 MPa point (+1.2 %)..

Model limitation, not a bug..
- `gs-c1nc5-344.26K-1.379MPa (grayson-streed)` — bubble_P -10.9 % (1.228 vs 1.379 MPa); y_C1 passes (0.7398 vs 0.7568) - Investigated 2026-11-04 (csgs): two data bugs fixed - methane omega_cs 0.011 -> 0 (Henley & Seader 1981 App. I p. 715; it had cut K_C1 by 11 %) and the GS simple-fluid A1 -2.10889 -> -2.10899 (H&S p. 188) - after which the implementation reproduces an independent 1966 Grayson-Streed implementation to its printed digits (Saxena thesis Table 5 p. 129, C1/nC4 at 310.93 K / 2.758 MPa: K_C1 5.73 vs 5.74, K_nC4 0.193 vs 0.193), and that published GS prediction is itself 15 % below the measured K_C1 6.75. At 310.93 K / 4.137 MPa both K stay low: K_C1 4.29 vs 4.93 (-13 %), K_nC5 0.0572 vs 0.0705 (-19 %); the GS pure-liquid nu0 of nC5 (0.0300) equals the PR pure-liquid f/P (0.0297), so the nC5 deficit is the correlation's Redlich-Kwong vapour fugacity of the heavy component (phi_V 0.526 vs PR 0.476). Model limitation of a correlation fitted for hydrogen-rich hydrotreater service, not a bug; lee-kesler-ploecker reproduces the 4.137 MPa point (+1.2 %)..

- `hasdemir2007-dcetol-101.3kPa-x0.27` — y_DCE 0.4516 vs 0.48 (abs 0.028, band 0.02); bubble_T ok (373.97 vs 374.85 K) - data quality suspected, not a model bug: the model sits on Raoult's law here (ideal-solution bubble T / y at the same x: 373.97 K / 0.452, 367.36 K / 0.695, 361.66 K / 0.870 with thermo's Psat), as the Kirss 2002 fit of this pair (near-ideal) implies; the Hasdemir & Uslu points imply gamma_DCE / gamma_toluene of 1.04/0.92, 0.94/0.85 and 0.86/1.08 at x_DCE 0.27/0.50/0.75 (activity coefficients crossing 1 in opposite directions, and bubble T 3-4 K above Raoult with y below it), which is not a consistent binary; no second open toluene + 1,2-dichloroethane set was found in the ThermoML archive to arbitrate (measured 2026-11-09).

- `margules-ig-pure-H2O-340K (margules_ig)` — Cp 70.2529 vs 75.4562 (-6.90%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. The liquid_reference caloric (wilson_lr_ig) meets these points (measured 2026-11-04).

- `nrtl-ig-etohh2o-azeotrope-101.325kPa` — bubble_T passes (352.054 vs 351.35 K, +0.20%); y_EtOH 0.9147 vs 0.8947 (+0.020 abs, just past the 0.02 band): the model's azeotrope sits at higher ethanol than measured - predictive-model deviation, no fitted parameter (measured 2026-11-04).
- `nrtl-ig-meohh2o-101.325kPa-349.05K (cosmo_sac_ig)` — bubble_T passes (350.406 vs 349.05 K, +0.39%); y_MeOH 0.6870 vs 0.7197 (-0.033 abs vs 0.02) misses. Predictive model with no fitted binary parameter: COSMO-SAC 2010 without the dispersion term under-predicts methanol's activity in water here; no bug found (the model reproduces the Bell et al. 2020 benchmark ln gamma to 1e-6, tests/thermo/test_cosmo_sac.py) (measured 2026-11-04).
- `nrtl-ig-meohh2o-101.325kPa-349.05K (nrtl)` — y 0.6991 vs 0.7197 (abs 0.021 > 0.02) - Gao (2012) y is CALCULATED (indirect T,p,x,HmE method), not measured; with the liquid phi_sat now carried by the real-vapour pairings (fix 7c5aca9) the databank pair lands ~0.01 lower in y_MeOH at this point and crosses the 0.02 band (the ideal-gas pairing of the same pair passes it); bubble T passes (measured 2026-11-04).

- `nrtl-ig-meohh2o-312.91K-20.705kPa (cosmo_sac_ig)` — bubble_P passes (20423.3 vs 20705 Pa, -1.4%); y_MeOH 0.7420 vs 0.8053 (-0.063 abs) misses: the same under-predicted methanol activity in water as the Gao 101.325 kPa point (measured 2026-11-04).

- `nrtl-ig-pure-H2O-340K (nrtl_ig)` — Cp 70.2529 vs 75.4562 (-6.90%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. The liquid_reference caloric (wilson_lr_ig) meets these points (measured 2026-11-04).

- `nrtl-ig-pure-MeOH-330K (nrtl_ig)` — rho_V 0.869469 vs 0.911218 (-4.58%, band 3.0%); Cp 73.1651 vs 88.5047 (-17.33%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. - `sle-anthracene-benzene-298.15K-acree` — solubility +36.7 % (ideal 0.009746 vs IUPAC-NIST evaluated 0.00713 at 298.15 K, Acree 1994 evaluation, sysID 58_57). Model limitation, not a bug: anthracene in benzene is strongly non-ideal (gamma ~ 1.37 at saturation); the ideal-solubility row claims gamma = 1 and carries no activity model, and the fusion constants are the CRC/databank tabulated values (Tm 489.15 K, Hfus 29.4 kJ/mol, consistent with NIST WebBook Tfus 490 K and Goursot et al. 29.37 kJ/mol). Measured 2026-11-04..

- `sulfinol-macgregor1988-t5.6-r01` — K_CO2 38.0308 vs 19.7952 (+92.1 %), K_H2S 21.2835 vs 13.5293 (+57.3 %) - Deshmukh-Mather reconstruction of MacGregor 1988 with Table 6.4 constants: over Table 5.6 the K error is mean |ln| 0.33 for CO2 (bias +0.21, low-loading rows up to 2.3x high) and 0.31 for H2S (H2S-rich rows 30-40 % low). The thesis's own model ran consistently high at 40 C on these mixed data with Table 6.4 (p. 67) and the reconstruction misses the fitted single-gas tables by mean |ln p| 0.55 CO2 / 0.29 H2S, so this is the model's level plus reconstruction choices where the scan is silent (K(MDEA prot.) as a base constant, ln-base A on water density, aqueous K_w); not a solver fault (speciation balances and the flash identity are pinned by tests/thermo/test_deshmukh_mather.py); measured 2026-11-09.

- `t1r-nrtl-etohh2o-101.3kPa-352.73K-x0.543 (vanlaar_hoc)` — y_EtOH 0.6929 vs 0.669 (abs 0.0239, band 0.02) - model limitation, not a bug: the two-parameter, T-independent van Laar pair (data/thermo_params/vanlaar/pairs.yaml etohh2o) is fitted to the single 1-atm azeotrope point only, so it does not carry the dilute-ethanol non-ideality (y_EtOH low by 0.04-0.06 and bubble_T high by about 0.6 % at x_EtOH <= 0.1) and overshoots y by 0.02-0.03 at x_EtOH 0.39-0.54; the NRTL rows meet these points (Lai 2014 via ThermoML, measured 2026-11-09).

- `uniquac-ig-pure-H2O-340K (uniquac_ig)` — Cp 70.2529 vs 75.4562 (-6.90%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. The liquid_reference caloric (wilson_lr_ig) meets these points (measured 2026-11-04).

- `uniquac-ig-pure-MeOH-330K (uniquac_ig)` — rho_V 0.869469 vs 0.911218 (-4.58%, band 3.0%); Cp 73.1651 vs 88.5047 (-17.33%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. - `wilson-ig-pure-H2O-340K` — Cp 70.2529 vs 75.4562 (-6.90%, band 5.0%) - model limitation, not a bug: the vapour-route caloric (thermo GibbsExcessLiquid default) builds liquid H as H_ig - RT^2 dlnPsat/dT (ideal-gas Clausius-Clapeyron: no vapour non-ideality, no Poynting), so Cp_L = Cp_ig - d/dT(RT^2 dlnPsat/dT); the same number follows from CoolProp's own Psat (H2O 340 K: 70.24 vs 75.46 J/mol/K), and the error grows with T. The liquid_reference caloric (wilson_lr_ig) meets these points (measured 2026-11-04).

## How to add a case

1. Add an entry to `data/validation/cases.yaml` (`binary_cases`/`multicomponent_cases`) with `id`, `package`, `components`, `z`, `T` (and/or `P`), `expected` (`vf`, `rho_V`, `rho_L`, `H`, `S`, `Cp`, `bubble_P`, `dew_P`, `bubble_T`, `K`, `vapor_comp`, `liquid_comp`), a `source` with authors, journal, year, table/page and retrieval date, and — only where the spec's fixed policy does not apply — a `tolerance`.
2. Pure-fluid points: add a `pure_cases` entry, then run `uv run python scripts/validate_properties.py --regen-coolprop` to fill `expected`.
3. Run `uv run python scripts/validate_properties.py --write-doc`, then commit `cases.yaml`, `results.json` and `docs/validation.md` together. `tests/validation/test_reference_cases.py` picks the case up automatically.

Never loosen a tolerance to make a case pass: a failing case is assessed (model limitation vs bug) and documented, not tuned away.
